caption: The drawing depicts an ornate religious altar set against a pale, marble-textured wall. The altar structure is symmetrically arranged with three main vertical compartments, supported by four columns that have gold-colored Corinthian capitals and bases. In the central niche, there is a statue of Jesus with a crown of thorns, arms bound, and draped in a white robe, holding a reed. On either side, in smaller niches, are statues of two male saint figures in brown robes, each on a small pedestal. Above the central statue is an arched space decorated with a pair of gold and blue angel wings and floral motifs. The altar top has a semi-circular pediment, inside of which is an illustration of two cherubs holding a shield with a blue cross and gold crown, surrounded by a blue and green border. The altar table is covered with a green cloth with white lace trim, the words “Agnus Dei” (Lamb of God) are visible. On top of the table is a crucifix flanked by two gold candlesticks. The floor in front of the altar is terracotta-colored tile, and a reddish carpet leads up to the altar. The color palette consists mainly of blue, gold, white, pale pink, green, brown, and terracotta hues, with decorative floral and geometric patterns accenting the composition. The artist’s signature appears in the lower right corner.
title: Side Altar, San Luis Rey Mission
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
